newsitem.title: USA: Long Beach, Calif., OKs bond refinancing plan.
newsitem.headline: Long Beach, Calif., OKs bond refinancing plan.

text.p: Long Beach, California's city council has adopted a refinancing plan for a series of earthquake repair bonds that went into default in 1996, city officials said on Monday.

Under the plan, bondholders will receive the full amount of their investments. Their interest will also be paid in full with the exception of the last 10 months when the interest will be about three percent less, officials said.
The refinancing calls for assessment liens and penalties to be securitized in the form of bonds, according to Stone & Youngberg LLC, which fashioned the workout plan.

The city of Long Beach will buy about $7 million of the bonds so it can both receive the delinquent payments with penalties and achieve liquidity by selling its position to outside investors as delinquencies are brought current.

"The securitized penalties and tougher remedial provisions that Stone & Youngberg fashioned give the city of Long Beach an excellent chance to recover our investment plus interest and make bondowners whole," Long Beach Treasurer Dick Hilde said in a statement.
The bonds were originally issued to help property-owners seismically strengthen their buildings in downtown Long Beach.
